utterances.text: Mr. Robson, I personally have a problem with this number 51, and the comment that is made below that in this document. Are you able to give guidance to this Chamber about that entry number 51 and the comment there which is not part of this gentleman's handwritten document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: I would make two points Your Honour. First of all, what we saw in the last paragraph of the document, and it is not on the page that front much us, is that there was reference to a list being attached to the requested that was sent to the Bosnian authorities. We don't know what that list is, but I would hazard a guess that it was Mr. Karahasanovic's list, because we have the information that's been provided on it; and then this document goes in to comment upon that list that was provided to say that the entries at items 7 and 57 are not the same. So whoever prepared the Ministry of Defence has drawn a conclusion that those two persons are one and the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And then decides to substitute the one with another name which we don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: We don't know how that name arose, Your Honour. But, again, that is a matter that goes to weight, I would submit. It is a discrepancy; but looking at the number of names listed on it, it is one of 51.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It doesn't sound to me like a discrepancy. It sounds to me like a deliberate, intended alteration by the person who authored this document, because that this person comes to the conclusion that number 7 and number 51 are one and the same person. So he intends to change the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm not in a position to speculate on that, but what he would be say is that this witness has been able to explain the process by which he prepared his list, and obviously --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm happy with this witness's list. I'm not happy with this list.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, the point is that at this stage we're considering admissibility, and we would say that there's a clear link between this witness and the Ministry of Defence document. Discrepancies and problems with this document are obviously matters that can be explored at a later stage when you come to consider the weight and relevance of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is there a relationship between this witness and the document or is it just a relationship between the witness and some of the contents of this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would suggest there was -- there is a clear link. You have the witness preparing his list; and then on the basis of that, you have this document we see in front of us prepared some 11 years later. It is clear that the author of this document had another document in front of him. The list was attached to the request, he states. It's -- this has followed on as a result of Mr. Karahasanovic preparing his initial list in 1995, we would submit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If the list, and we don't know what list that is, if the list was accompanied this document, why was it necessary to re-list the people in this document? It could have been a very short document just saying fine, enclosed herewith the list that we received of the people, instead of re-listing them and then changing some of them or at least one of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Again, Your Honour, that is an area I wouldn't like to speculate upon. I would like to mention is that if we refer to the indictment, what you will see in the indictment is an annex of the names of the Serb prisoners of war who were alleged to have been killed in 1995. And in that document, there is reference to the names as mentioned in Mr. Karahasanovic's list and also this document. So this, we would say, is a key document relating to the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: In the indictment, does the name at number 51 in this document appear?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I apologise, because I do not have the indictment do hand. Your Honour, what you will see is that there are 52 entries in the indictment: 51 bears the surname Cupeljic, 52 is Marko Maric. So it seems that the Prosecution are hedging their bets and going for both versions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Sartorio.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I would just like to add to a few of -- if the Chamber is inclined to admit this document, that there are a series of other documents, internal documents that the Defence is well aware of, and that we move to add to our exhibit list, those documents. Those documents shed doubt on some of the -- on the accuracy of some of the information in this document. So Mr. Robson has mentioned, on a couple of occasions in his argument to admit the document, the word "speculation": I can't speculate, I can't speculate. That is exactly what we are doing, speculating here about who made this document, what it was made from, what its purpose was for, et cetera, et cetera. There is no evidence that we used this list in drafting the indictment either. There is no evidence that the list was attached either. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let's also, from the Prosecution side, Madam Sartorio, not embellish what has been said here. Nobody has speculated about who drafted this document, what it was made from, and what its purpose was.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: No. I didn't say he was speculating, Your Honour. I used the word "speculation" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: No. You said: "So Mr. Robson has mentioned, on a couple of occasions in his argument to admit the document, the word 'speculation': I can't speculate, I can't speculate. That is exactly what we are doing here about who made this document, what it was made from, what its purpose was for." This is what you are saying.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I'm just arguing that to admit this document would be based often speculation. I wasn't implying that we're speculating.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Robson, I have a difficulty with this document, not because of the inaccuracy about the Cupeljic name. That has some very practical explanation. My difficulty is different, because what this document shows is that somehow the information included in the witness's list was finally registered in the Ministry of Defence, in the leadership of the ABiH. That suggests that the information about the capture of these prisoners was brought up through the system somehow, and I think this would be the point that the Prosecution wants to prove, that the information was relayed. So my question to you is: Do you have any information about how the witness's list ultimately was turned into this document? That's the link I need.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, the witness is here, so I'm loathe to say very much in the presence of the witness. What I will say is that you will recall that we've heard a previous witness who dealt with this document, and that witness - and I can name the person if necessary - that person explained how he received this document and what he did with the document. It may very well be that the question that you are putting to me, Your Honour, has been dealt with by that witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I shall have to look back into that witness's statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Yes. The Presiding Judge suggests that, to the extent which this witness can provide us that same information, then that would be a corroboration.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I, too, would like to say this. I have a problem. Actually, I have two problems, especially so with the issue of the link with this witness. If I understood properly, I stand to be corrected. If I didn't, that's the link between two lists. The witness made a list, he knows it, he can speak about it. With regard to the list, unfortunately, there's no matching, there are doubts, strong doubts. There is no link with the comments, if I understood properly. I fail to see with regard to the link and with regard to the prima facie reliability how it can be established. Because of this difference, I find it difficult to admit the document. Can I have further explanations? I would be grateful, Mr. Robson.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Robson, you have two issues now: One from Judge Harhoff and another from Judge Lattanzi. Would you like to deal with them sequentially?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Thank you. I think the only way really to properly deal with Judge Harhoff's question is to put a further question to the witness. So with your leave, I'll do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: As you please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Mr. Karahasanovic, do you know how the information contained in your list has come to appear in a document generated by the Ministry of Defence of Bosnia and Herzegovina in 2006?

utterances.speaker: IZET KARAHASANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't. I only know that I drafted the report and sent it to the brigade. As from that point onwards, I know nothing of the list or the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: I don't think I can take that point any further. Turning to Judge Lattanzi's question, the first point I'd like to make is that the Defence came into receipt of this document prior to the trial commencing, and it was a document supplied by the Prosecution. So the Defence`s opportunities to inquire into the reliability of the list have been rather limited. However, it is clear that the names contained within the Ministry of Defence list constitute a key part of the indictment, and the Defence was extremely keen to try and find out more about this document. We believe it is relevant and has probative value. However, the question of weight is obviously a matter for the Judges, and also that would relate to liability as well. We would say it has sufficient prima facie reliability for it to be admitted at this stage. Just on that point, perhaps we could say -- I apologise, Judge Lattanzi.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robson, you only answered one part of my question. I had another problem, that of the link with this witness, because this issue could be dealt with through another witness who could provide further information or explanations. The issue of the link with this witness, I wanted to hear from you because maybe I didn't understand it. Is it a connection on the mere basis of this list, because if it is on the list as such, then the issue of the reliability is sort of -- comes after is that of the link.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, if this had been a document bearing only a fraction of the names contained on Mr. Karahasanovic's list, it would be difficult to argue with you. But here we have almost identically the same names listed. These were people that this witness spoke to. He has been able to comment today on the substance of the Ministry of Defence report. He has been able to explain how he obtained the names and details, and he's been able to comment on what the Ministry of Defence understood to be a discrepancy or a duplication between entry 7 and 51. In my submission, he -- the link is clear. This document clearly flows from the list produced by Mr. Karahasanovic, and he is in a position to comment on the substance of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So from the point of view of the list, we just need the list provided by the witness. We do not need this one, because we don't flow whether this one is reliable or not because there is no connection, no matching. He was the first to draft this list. Therefore, if the Ministry of Defence received the list, it received it on the basis of this list. So the comment -- the comment is not connected to the witness, so I still fail to see the connection with that list or that document. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Perhaps just my final point on reliability. That is that, at this stage, the Trial Chamber only need be satisfied that there is a prima facie indicia of reliability. If we look at the document, the source is clear. It's from the authorities of Bosnia and Herzegovina. There's a name upon the document, it was stamped, it was sent to our colleagues at the Office of the Prosecution, who forwarded the document on to us. So we would submit that the prima facie indicia are satisfied.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted by majority; Judge Lattanzi dissenting.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Mr. Karahasanovic, I want to take you back to your list. What did you do with the list once you prepared it, if you could remind us once again?

utterances.speaker: IZET KARAHASANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The list I drew up, as I said, was sent to the brigade and another copy was given to my commander for his records. I sent it to the brigade to the assistant commander for security, i.e., my superior.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And what was his name?

utterances.speaker: IZET KARAHASANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Enes Malcibegovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Do you know whether Mr. Malcibegovic did anything with the information that you sent to him?

utterances.speaker: IZET KARAHASANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the system of command and control, I have no right to ask my superior whether he did so or not. I know that when I attended one of the monthly brigade meetings, I saw the documents I had sent in the office. When we discussed those, he said that it had been processed and that the list had reached him. As for what he did further, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If I may just interrupt, Mr. Robson. The MFI 651 that was admitted will be given Exhibit number 651.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And do you know whether, based on the information that you sent, the military security service conducted any investigation [Realtime transcript read in error "information"]?

utterances.speaker: IZET KARAHASANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, they did not. Had they done so, I would have known. The only person who was following those events was myself; therefore, they should have called me in to tell them what I knew. I don't know whether they followed it up whatsoever, but no one asked me anything about that case of again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: While Mr. Robson is consulting, I just want to say that, at page 53, line 4, the list word should be "investigation" and not "information."

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Do you know who should have conducted the investigation, if one was to be carried out?

utterances.speaker: IZET KARAHASANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The investigation should have been conducted by the security service of the brigade and the military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And you said that -- and who was the commander of the security service -- no, sorry. Apart from the assistant commander for security, you said that you sent the document to the commander. Who was the person that you sent it to?

utterances.speaker: IZET KARAHASANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I sent it to my battalion commander, Ahmed Sehic. I also sent the report to the assistant commander for security, Enes Malcibegovic. He was the assistant commander for security of the 328th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Finally, on this point, who was the commander of the brigade?

utterances.speaker: IZET KARAHASANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander of the 328th Brigade was Fuad Zilkic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, the last document I wish to use is Exhibit 480. Your Honours, while we're waiting for the document, I can explain that this is a regular daily combat report dated 13th September 1995 from the 328th Mountain Brigade to the 35th Division. If we can just look at the final page in the document to see who it is from. That's page 5 in the English and page 4 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Are you able to see who this document is from?

utterances.speaker: IZET KARAHASANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Brigade Commander Fuad Zilkic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And he is the person you just told us was the commander of the 328th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: IZET KARAHASANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: I'd like to show you an entry on page 3 of the English version and page 2 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: If we can scroll down in the B/C/S version, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Do you see point number 4?

utterances.speaker: IZET KARAHASANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And, there, there's an entry that says: "On the 11th of September, 1995, two companies of the 5th Battalion of the 328th Brigade captured 61 hostiles and three Serbian women in the Kesten village sector. Members of the El Mujahedin Unit took charge of all the captives except two, while the two were turned over to the 328th Brigade military police. A large number of fire-arms were captured in this action, about which we will submit a report later." Is this the information that you sent to Mr. Malcibegovic?

utterances.speaker: IZET KARAHASANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. First of all, they were taken prisoner on the 10th of September. It is correct that it was done by the 2nd Company in the Kesten area, but the number was not 61. We had 51 captured. And as for the two mentioned that were subsequently handed over to the military police of the 328th, I don't know where that came from. When I drafted my report and the list, it reads "51," not "61." Here, it says they were handed over. They were not. They were taken away forcefully. This sort of a report for a commander who was supposed to have undergone military training would not be a good report. I don't see a point in this.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sir, on Exhibit 646, your handwritten list, below the 51 people, you wrote "4 Arapi, 3 women," and a few things, and then right at the bottom was a total of 62, encircled. What did that mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It means that, on that day, there were 62.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's right. This one here gives 61 plus one. Was that taken, killed, or something like that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It says 61 hostiles and three Serbian women, plus two who were turned over to the military police. In total, that would be more than the one I wrote down.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And on the list we saw earlier, where it was written "62," did you write the word "62"?

utterances.speaker: IZET KARAHASANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I wasn't adding anything up. I wrote the things I did, and I indicated those I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And when you gave your report to Mr. Malcibegovic, did you mention who had taken the prisoners of war?

utterances.speaker: IZET KARAHASANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In my report, it states that the Arabs took the POWs away by force. We did not hand them over to them, as one would clue from this document. We had problems with them, and we should have physically opposed them to prevent them from doing that; however, we did not and they were taken away by force.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: In your report to Mr. Malcibegovic, did you say that they were taken away by the El Mujahedin Unit?

utterances.speaker: IZET KARAHASANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We called everyone there Arabs. We used the "El Mujahedin" term infrequently. All people who differed from us, whose complexion was darker than ours, we used to call them Arabs.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Robson. Madam Sartorio.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Would this be a good time for us to take a break, Your Honours, or would you want me to proceed for five minutes?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If you so command, we will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Can I just ask put one question.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Based on this document, Mr. Witness, did you see this report at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. This report was shown to me for the first time by an investigator in Sarajevo. I think his name was Mr. Majik, or so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: My interest is to know if you were able to form an opinion then, in September 1995, about the correctness of the information that was sent up, further up into the system. You have pointed to two or three important differences here today, by saying that it is an inaccuracy, or a misstatement really, that the witness were turned over because that was not the case. They were not turned over, they were forcefully taken from you. Also, there is the issue of who they were turned over to or who took them, because the document says that it was the El Mujahed Detachment. But you, in your report, never stated any such thing. So, here, we have two significant inaccuracies. My question to you is: At the time, in September 1995, did you hear anything or were you able to suspect that the information that you had passed on was incorrectly passed on from further up into the system? Do you understand my question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe I did. I sent the report the way I did. I don't know in what form my superiors sent it upwards. I cannot see what my superior wrote. That is not something that I can demand of him. He was my superior. It was up to him to order me what to do and not the other way around. It wasn't his duty to show me his report. My duty, when I draft a report, is to forward it to him, and then he know what is I had written.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I understand that perfectly. But my question is: Really, did you discuss it with him, or did you ever talk about these incidents again, you and your commander and the assistant commander in the brigade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. As I said a moment ago, when I attended a monthly meeting, I asked him whether that report of mine reached him. I also saw the documents I sent attached to the report, whereby he told me that, indeed, he received it and that it was his problem from that point on. That was the end of the conversation. We didn't discuss it any further at a meeting, because there was other agenda to be discussed at the meeting. That was the last we talk about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just one question, sir. Within the system of command and control, is it possible that a senior, on compiling a report, does so based on more than one source, if there may be?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. When drafting a report, since all battalions sent their reports into the brigade -- based on all battalion reports sent to the brigade received by a superior at the brigade, he compiles his own report that he then sends further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And this report comes from all these battalions, various sources?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Maybe this is a convenient time to take the break. We'll come back at half past 12.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Sartorio.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir. I will be asking you some questions on behalf of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Could we please bring up Exhibit 480 again.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And while we're waiting for the exhibit to come up, I'd like to ask you, as an assistant commander of security of a battalion, wasn't it one of your responsibilities to be on the scene as soon as possible after POWs were captured?

utterances.speaker: IZET KARAHASANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because I don't know what happened in what area or what might happen in what area. I would go where ever I was called to. I was at the forward command post where -- which was the closest to any place where something might have happened and where I might have been called to in the area of the 5th Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: But it was -- it would be important for you to learn about the existence of POWs, so that you could interview them to get information about what the enemy troops may be doing, because your job was to -- was to make sure and to keep charge of security of the troops. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: IZET KARAHASANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because, naturally, I was supposed to. But since there was a large group of those prisoners, I couldn't have interviewed them. If there had been one or two, I could have interviewed them and asked them what unit they belonged to. But as for any further questions as to what their units was doing and so on, I did not have the appropriate training to obtain this kind of information. There were other officers in the brigade who had the appropriate training, and they would have taken their statements.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I'm not talking this particular instance. I'm asking, in general, as assistant commander for security, wouldn't you be informed very early if there were POWs captured, so that you could take measures to go see those POWs and to get information from them which might impact the security of the troops.

utterances.speaker: IZET KARAHASANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since I did not have any prisoners of war before, and I never talked to any or couldn't take any statements from them, that was the first instance; and, suddenly, I faced 51 prisoners, and I did what was the safest, the most expeditious, and the best solution for both for me, my men, and the prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now with regard to Exhibit 480, could we scroll down to the paragraph that was discussed on direct examination, please. It's, I believe, four. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, sir, are you aware of any capture of any prisoners Serbian troops and three Serbian women on the 11th of September by two companies of the 5th Battalion of the 328th Brigade, anywhere in the area of Kesten, other than the incident that has been the subject of your testimony on direct examination?

utterances.speaker: IZET KARAHASANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All I know is that of our company because we couldn't move and we couldn't get information from other battalions. And, in our battalion, the only thing that happened was that this company of ours captured 51 people and the other persons that I noted down: Four that were taken by the Arab, three women, and two that he were kill.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: But, again, the question is a just a simple yes or no. Are you aware of the capture of any other prisoners and three Serbian women that day by anyone in the 5th Battalion? That's a yes or no, sir.

utterances.speaker: IZET KARAHASANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in the 5th Battalion, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. Are you aware of capture of prisoners by any other battalion on that day?

utterances.speaker: IZET KARAHASANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: May the witness please be shown Exhibit 466. May I have one moment, Your Honour, or just a few minutes, please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: -- with the Court's indulgence. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours, four your indulgence.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, sir, can you tell us the date of this document and can you tell us who it is from and who it is going to?

utterances.speaker: IZET KARAHASANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 10th of September, 1995. It is sent to the commander of the 328th Mountain Brigade, 4th Manoeuvre, 2nd Manoeuvre, and OD El Mujahed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And what is the subject of this order -- or the subject of this document is what, sir?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Could we have the English part of this scrolled down, so that we can reed it, too.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I was getting to that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Could you tell us what this says at the top of the left? What is the substance of this order, sir?

utterances.speaker: IZET KARAHASANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean, "based on the assessment of the situation and success achieved in the assault on the basis of plan, illegible, 95, and in order to reinforce and secure the results achieved ..." I really don't know what that means.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Well, this is an order that is engaging certain troops in certain places, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Robson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. The Prosecution is inviting the witness to comment on the document. It first needs to be established that this witness had some knowledge of the matters contained in this document. We can see it's from the 35th Division to a number of units which do not include the 5th Battalion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Sartorio.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Well, if could scroll down to the part of the document that I want to ask the witness about.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Sir, isn't it true that the El Mujahedin Detachment operated in the area of the 328th Brigade in September of 1995 as part of Operation Farz?

utterances.speaker: IZET KARAHASANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if the El Mujahedin did. I know that there were Arabs in this area, in the area of responsibility of the 328th. But now as whether it was the El Mujahedin Unit or not, I don't know. I know that they were moving around that area. They would go out to the line. Because, for instance, if I went to visit, to tour the defence lines, the soldiers who were there would tell me that Arabs had come in, that they had gone on a reconnaissance mission, and things of that nature. But I don't know any other things.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. Well, rather than comment on the document, I'd like to scroll up for just a minute and all I want to do is --

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: In the English, please, sorry. Scroll up in English, down in Bosnian. No. The top of the second page, please. Well, sorry. It's the bottom of the first page, in English. Number 8 is what I need to read from the beginning. Second page, sorry. It is three pages, long. The bottom of the second page.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Sir, would you agree with me that this says: "Forces of the El Mujahedin Detachment shall be kept for intervention in the ..."

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Could you please go to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: "... area of responsibility of the 328th Brigade in accordance with the following disposition: Part of the forces along the defence line in the sector of Kesten village, Kosa village, and Prokop." Would you agree me that that's what this says here?

utterances.speaker: IZET KARAHASANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is what the document says.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to you remember the three names, Kesten, Kosa and Prokop, if you would.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: This document may be put away, and I would like map number 19 to be brought up from the court binder. If you could, yes, enlarge it considerably. Maybe one more enlargement, if you could. No. That's it. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Sir, on this map, can you tell us where Kesten is?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Could we have assistance for him to mark it, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. Could you put a 1 there, please?

utterances.speaker: IZET KARAHASANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Now do you see Koso on this map -- Kosa, K-O-S-A?

utterances.speaker: IZET KARAHASANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kosa is further down. I think that's where it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And could you circle it, please, and put a 2.

utterances.speaker: IZET KARAHASANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. Now, sir, do you see Prokop - I apologise if I have mispronounced it - Prokop on the map anywhere?

utterances.speaker: IZET KARAHASANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that's where it is, just below Pejanovici, here.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: IZET KARAHASANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Should I put a 3 next to it?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: IZET KARAHASANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: So would it be fair to say that the area -- that is the area that was just the subject matter of the order, the part of the order that we just read, and that those three names were mentioned as being an area where the El Mujahedin were to be prepared to intervene?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Robson --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is the mention of those three names in the report.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now I'm going to work further with this map with regard to another exhibit. I need another moment, Your Honours, for just one second.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: It's P0 2715, Your Honours. May this document be brought up, and we'll put the map aside for the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Wait a minute. You can't put it aside. It will be erased.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: If we freeze, it are we able to bring it back and then rewrite on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You've got admit it; otherwise, you're going to loose this.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Well, I want to add it but I want to add further --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, you'd better add those things, because once you move it, these things are gone.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: All right. I'll add them.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Sir, on this map, do you see where Durica [sic] is?

utterances.speaker: IZET KARAHASANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Durici.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you for correcting my pronunciation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: There is Djurica Vis on the map and there is Durici. Which one do you want, Madam?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Durici or Djurica? What do you want?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Djurica Vis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Then that is not Durici. Those are two different places.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you for pointing that out.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Djurica Vis, please?

utterances.speaker: IZET KARAHASANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Could you please point it out and make a 4.

utterances.speaker: IZET KARAHASANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Sir, do you see where Visic is, the Visic facility, elevation 497? Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: IZET KARAHASANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is it further up from here? I think it is more or less.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Let me ask you this: Do you know see, on this map, Gornji [sic]?

utterances.speaker: IZET KARAHASANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Gornjani, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Could you please mark that - thank you - and put a 5.

utterances.speaker: IZET KARAHASANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now do you know -- again, I'll ask the question giving the reference of Gornjani. Do you know where elevation 497 and the Visic facility might be?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I just ask a question, Madam Sartorio. You are cross-examining.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And this map book has been admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Why don't you just lead the witness and tell him where these places are.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I will, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Then you will save more time.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I can, but this is not labelled on the map, so I do not want to mislead the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Is it near Jasik? Is it near that area, sir, if you know?

utterances.speaker: IZET KARAHASANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kasike. It says "Kasike" on the map. Is that what you're asking me about?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I'm asking you about Visic, elevation 497.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Can we make it larger or not. All right. I will move on if this witness is not able to identify this particular area.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I can't see Visic here.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: May this be admitted as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Robson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. All that the Prosecution has asked the witness to do is to identify places on the map that have been told to him. There's has been no questions about the relevance of those places, whether he has been there, whether anything happened there. So all we have is a document with some circles and a number, and it is my submission that it doesn't have any relevance or probative value.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I would imagine, Madam Sartorio, that Mr. Robson is talking specifically with respect to 4 and 5.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes. That's why I'm going to freeze it and then show the witness a document that relates to 4 and 5.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, but he wants to get from you the relevance of 4 and 5.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I can't remove this from the screen to show the relevance because I will loose it. And so you can mark it marked for identification now, freeze it, we'll go to the document, and then I will move that it be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is marked for identification. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the map will become Exhibit number 1353, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now may the witness be shown PT 2715 -- PO, sorry. It's P0 2715.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, sir, this document purports to be dated the 24th of August, 1995. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I see --

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: It's a range of dates, yes. The 24th of August to the 10th of October.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just wait a minute. The document that we have is dated the 14th of October.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes. It is dated the 14th.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Sorry, sir. It is regarding activities between the 24th of August and the 10th of October, 1995. Is that what it says in this document? Is that what it says.

utterances.speaker: IZET KARAHASANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're asking me?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: IZET KARAHASANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat it. I didn't understand it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: My question is: Does this document say that it is an analysis of combat actions between 24 August and 10 October of 1995?

utterances.speaker: IZET KARAHASANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's what it says here on the top.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I'd like to scroll down to 2.2, please, in both the English and B/C/S. Now, 2.2, please, in English. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, at the very bottom of the page, sir, well, in the English, there's a time of day mentioned, 0900 hours. Do you see that in your document in section 2.2?

utterances.speaker: IZET KARAHASANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 2.2, I can't see 0900 hours anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Could you go to the next page in B/C/S, please, at the top, please. No, not in English; in B/C/S. Leave the English one where it was, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: It's approximately eight lines down from the top the page, sir. Do you see the time 0900 hours?

utterances.speaker: IZET KARAHASANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. Now does the document say at 0900 hours: "On 11 September 1995, the 3rd Manoeuvre Company ..."

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And you need to scroll --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. It says: "On the next day, the 11th of September 1995, at 0900 hours, the 3rd Manoeuvre," I guess.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. Can you keep going?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Can you change over the page in English, please, so the Judges can read.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Could you finish that sentence, sir: The 3rd Manoeuvre Company ..."

utterances.speaker: IZET KARAHASANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "... the 3rd Manoeuvre, together with the El Mujahedin Detachment, took the features in the Vis sector and linked up with the forces of the 2nd Manoeuvre Battalion and elements of the 222nd Mountain Brigade. The fighters of the 3/2 Manoeuvre," I guess, "Battalion are in the Vis sector, and they flew the flag of Bosnia and Herzegovina."

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: So this, what you just read - and I don't believe you said Vis - does it say "Djurica Vis"?

utterances.speaker: IZET KARAHASANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Vis," and there's is no "Djurica." Well, there is some kind of a mark there, like a line; but it doesn't say "Djurica," it says "Uri."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Robson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. Prosecution counsel has been asking a number of questions about this document for a while now. The units that the document refers to are the 3rd Manoeuvre Company and also the 2nd Manoeuvre Company. My understanding is that that has got nothing to do with the 328th brigade. The objection is that the Prosecution counsel should be putting questions of relevance to the witness, in order to establish a link between him and the -- a question of relevance between him and this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Sartorio.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will be going over a number of points with this witness, statements that he has made in his prior statements about the El Mujahedin operating in the area of the 328th Brigade. This is a document, at the same time, that shows where the El Mujahedin is operating. All I'm asking him is to tell me whether the document say what is it says, and he has made a map for us to set the foundation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I just hold on, Madam Sartorio.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Sartorio, I know I cut you short in the middle of responding to an objection, but the Registry advises us that we have got a bit of a technical problem. That map with villages 1 to 5 is not retrievable up to the fifth village, but we can have it with villages 1, 2, 3. Are you likely to want it in the near future, while AV are still busy trying to get the problem sorted out. If you are wanting that exhibit, it is not going to be easy to get it back.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I think for this purpose, the Judges have seen the map and the places that were indicated, so I trust that can you remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You have real trust in our memory. That's fine. Now can you go back to the objection, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honour, I can ask get to this document later or I can get to it now, but I think that overall it will become clear, from the questions that I'm going to ask him about previous statements that he has made, that there is a connection between his testimony and prior statements and this particular document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Sartorio. You see, I can understand why Mr. Robson is objecting. You got to first establish a basis before you ask the witness to show you villages in a map, rather than asking for the villages to be shown and then say "I will show that link later." If you put a basis for your questions about the map, in that way you establish the link. You seem to be putting the cart before the horse.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I was trying to save time, Your Honour. I will go back --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You see, now you haven't.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I will put this document away, and I will proceed with questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes. Please establish that link; and then when you show him the document, then at least we know why you are asking [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Sir, you have provided a number of statements to the ICTY. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: IZET KARAHASANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And each time you have provided a statement, you have been allowed to read -- statements have been read back to you in your language, and you have signed and approved those documents -- those statements. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: IZET KARAHASANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When I gave statements to the investigators, the interpreter who was there interpreted to me what was written down, and I signed it as such. I never read a statement for myself because it was never given to me in Bosnian. It was read out to me by the interpreter from the laptop, and then I would sign the hard copy.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. Now, it's true that, in your statements, you have mentioned on several occasions that the El Mujahedin Detachment operated in the area of the 328th Brigade during Operation Farz in September 1995? Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: IZET KARAHASANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That Arab unit was in the area. Occasionally, it was within the area of the 328th Brigade, among others. I said, a moment ago, that those people, those Arabs, would come out to the front line. They would do there reconnaissance and all that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You are not being asked about the Arabs, sir. You are being asked about the El Mujahedin Detachment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. When I gave the statement and whenever I mentioned "Arabs," the investigator present would insist that that referred to the El Mujahedin Unit, and not to Arabs in general. We knew, when we saw an Arab, that he belonged to the El Mujahedin Unit. We presumed so, and that's why I said that it was the El Mujahedin Unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: May the witness be shown P0 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm getting confused here. You're giving us two positions. You are saying each time you said "Arab," the investigator insisted it was the El Mujahedin Detachment. In the same breath, you say each time you saw an Arab, you assumed it was an El Mujahedin Detachment, and that's why you said El Mujahedin Detachment. Which is which?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is correct. When the investigator talked to me about the topic, when I said "Arabs," that Arabs were active in the area, he would say, "No, not Arabs; that pertains to the El Mujahedin Unit." As I said, since I knew of no one else, no other Arabs, and that I only knew of the El Mujahedin Unit, I consented to that being introduced into the statement as such.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: May the witness be shown his statement, P0 6203.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: While we wait for that document to come up on screen, Mr. Witness, I just recall that this information that you have given us actually contradicts the information that you gave us earlier about not being able to identify the Arab that you saw in Kesten.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I told you what Arabs I saw. They had beards, loose clothes, and such. They had head gear. That's what I said I saw in Kesten, those Arabs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Well, maybe the question is really: If you knew that there were a separate unit of Arabs, which was called the El Mujahedin Detachment, were you aware of that fact or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I heard of the El Mujahid unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: And were you aware that this unit was a separate unit and that there were other Arab units?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I don't know how to ask the question. Are you able to form an opinion about the relation between the El Mujahedin Detachment and the 328th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know what the relation was between the El Mujahedin Detachment and the 328th. I was the assistant commander for security in the battalion, and I had nothing to do with that relation concerning the battalion commander, the brigade commander and the disposition of forces. I had to take care of my unit, concerning the security of the battalion, and I wasn't busying myself with the deployment of units and who was where at what time. We, the assistant commanders, did not attend commanders' meetings where they discussed things and made schedules and so on and so forth, and those things were not conveyed to the assistants.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I see. But when you actually met the Arabs in Kesten and they took away the prisoners of war from you, you must have asked yourself who these gentlemen were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. But who was I to ask? They were only shouting at us, holding us at gunpoint. I don't know what one can do at such a moment, when you are being threatened with a fire-arm. And if you're there with three or four soldiers of yourself, what can you do? They had no insignia, and you have no power to oppose them. What else can you do? There's no possibility for you to ask questions. They don't want to talk to you. They kept insisting, "Leave the room, leave the room," and that's it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Yes, I understand that. Did you subsequently try to find out who they were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I had no means to establish that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Well, I suppose you could have asked your commander.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The commander was notified; however, I don't think the commander knew who they were either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just would like to remind you what the witness said during examination-in-chief, because apart from the statement, the most important thing is what the witness said this morning. A question was asked on page 21, line 22, and here is the question: "Do you know what unit these Arabs belonged to, if they belonged to a unit at all? " The witness answered: "I want to stress that until then no one had named the Mujahedin." So the answer provided by the witness was very neutral in this respect. The witness said this: "No. I didn't know the unit they belonged to in our area. We knew there was the Mujahedin Unit." I'm translating from the English into French, and I'm sorry for this: "This was a rumour," that's how I understand the English, "and we did not know of any other unit that would have been in the area. Therefore, we thought that they were members of that unit, because we did not know if they were members of another unit." Therefore, during the examination-in-chief, independently, the witness of his own accord mentioned the El Mujahedin Unit, and I think that this is a reason or it justifies this link with the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, sir, do you recall -- strike that. The El Mujahedin Detachment had a camp at the 13th Kilometre, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: IZET KARAHASANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We heard of the existence of a camp. The rumour had it in the unit that there was a camp at the 13th Kilometre.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: But you told an investigator during an interview, September of 2006, at paragraph 51, you were very sure about who these people were who captured -- who took these POWs. You said: "The El Mujahedin came. They consisted of foreigners. They are the same units I spoke about previously in Livada Kamenica, at the 13th Kilometre where they had a camp." You seemed very sure at the time you made the statement, that that's who took the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: If you may go to paragraph 51, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: So my question to you, sir, that is the unit that took the prisoners, is it not?

utterances.speaker: IZET KARAHASANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said at the beginning, whenever I would say that these were Arabs, they insisted on that being the El Mujahid Unit. I didn't know whether there was any other Arab unit there, and I consented to that being the El Mujahed Unit. We heard of a camp at the 13th Kilometre towards Kamenica. Since we did not hear of any other place of -- of any other place that the captured or were taken, the presumption was that they took them to that camp; that is to say, if those people took away those prisoners, that they took them to the 13th Kilometre.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Well, it doesn't say anything here about where they took them. If you look at the statement, sir, did the -- did the investigator also tell you to say that the unit consisted of foreigners and that it was the same unit that you had spoken about previously in the Livade Kamenica at the 13th Kilometre? Did the investigator tell you to say that as well?

utterances.speaker: IZET KARAHASANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The unit was comprised of foreigners. We know there were Arabs. I explained to you what sort of people they were; however, they were slightly better kept, slightly better uniforms from what we could see when they would pass by in trucks. I was never with that unit, such as the one discussed here, the one called El Mujahedin. I never talked to them. I never attended a meeting with them and all that, so that I could tell you anything more about those people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Robson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, an issue of translation. I'm told that when the witness initially answered the question, he gave an immediate response to the question, which has not been captured and then went on to say the words which are on the transcript. So I think that should be clarified, his immediate response to the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sir, how did you start your answer to the question that was put to you? Can you repeat what you said earlier?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It had to do with the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I certainly don't want to suggest an answer to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Please don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: If we could just simply put the last part of the question: Did the investigator put that to you as well? Then if we could capture his answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Does the witness remember what is the what. Let's read the question to you. It was said to you: "Well, it doesn't say anything here about where they took them. If you look at the statement, sir, did the investigator also tell you to say that the unit consisted of foreigners and that it was same unit that you had spoken about previously in Livada Kamenica, at the 13th kilometre? Did the investigator tell you to say that as well?" Can you answer that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I was talking about the existence of ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well you have answered, and you said: "No." You were "talking about the existence of..." Can you finish that sentence, before I go to Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When I talked about this incident, I talked about Arabs. I repeat, upon the assistance of investigators, they asked me whether this concerned the El Mujahed Unit. I had no knowledge of any other units. I said, "possibly," since there were Arabs in that unit. Therefore, I believe that all the Arabs within the area of responsibility of the 328th belonged to the El Mujahed Unit. That is why I confirmed that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, thank you. I just wanted to ask you to allow the witness to complete his answer, but you have already done that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Madam Sartorio.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, leaving paragraph 51 for a moment, could we show the witness paragraph 26 of the statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, sir, in paragraph 26 you state: "They never participated in meetings at my level. The El Mujahedin Unit was a conquering, offensive force." Those were your words?

utterances.speaker: IZET KARAHASANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I never attended any meetings at that level. Since I was the assistant commander for security, I did not attend those. However, we did hear that they were an offensive unit and that they participated in combat.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. So going back to paragraph 51, again you referred to the unit called El Mujahed. So it is the same unit as you're talking about in 26, correct?

utterances.speaker: IZET KARAHASANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We are talking about the same unit. We keep referring to Arabs, and you keep insisting on that being the El Mujahed Unit. As I have said, when the investigators insisted, when I would say Arabs, I would sent six to seven hours working with them. They kept trying to convince me it was thank it was the El Mujahed Unit and not Arabs, and that all Arabs there belonged to that unit. Even today, I don't know whether all the Arabs there were in the area of the 328th coming there, whether they were all members of the El Mujahed Unit. These were Arabs for me and those other people I saw at the lines. I have no information of, say, Arabs participating here or as stated the unit. It's called the El Mujahedin Unit. I didn't deploy those units. I merely convey what happened I had told.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. One more question with regard to this statement, and it is in paragraph 56, if you would just take a moment to look at it. In this paragraph, sir, you are telling the investigator that -- you're referring to a document and that is the document referring to the POWs that were captured, and you said: "There's a description of 61 prisoners handed over to the El Mujahed Detachment." That is what is in your statement, correct?

utterances.speaker: IZET KARAHASANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what it is said in the statement, but I don't know how it was translated. I never said that we handed over anyone. Whenever I talked to the investigator, I kept stating the truth, which is that they were being taken forcefully. As for how it was translated, it is a different matter. When Her Honour the Judge was reading the transcript before, I could see that my words did not -- were not reflected in the interpretation. It wasn't what I had said and there were differences in interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Well, sir, do you remember in October of 2007 some members of the Office of the Prosecutor, as well as the Registry, came down to Sarajevo to meet with you?

utterances.speaker: IZET KARAHASANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was -- it was the date when Vanja was there and another lady, when I was signing the statements.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Right. And during that time-period, that took about a whole day, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: IZET KARAHASANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I stayed there for a long time reading the statements and making corrections.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And you --

utterances.speaker: IZET KARAHASANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- concerning translation and so on.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And you read your statements in the Bosnian language, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: IZET KARAHASANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And you made whatever corrections you thought were necessary at that time.

utterances.speaker: IZET KARAHASANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: More or less, all.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And I will be getting to that document eventually. But, now, at the end of your review, did you meet with a person from the Registry who then asked you a series of questions?

utterances.speaker: IZET KARAHASANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I came here in November, when I attended your proofing, I believe you talked to me here in The Hague, and not in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Right. I spoke with you in The Hague. But there were other people who spoke with you in Sarajevo, where we're talking about the time that you read all of your statements and made changes to the statements. Then you signed those statements on that day, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: IZET KARAHASANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vanja was there then, and another lady.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And you signed your statements in the Bosnian language on that day, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: IZET KARAHASANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And you certified that everything in those statements was true and correct before you signed, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: IZET KARAHASANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: More or less, so.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And you were asked by the person in the registry a series of questions outside of the hearing of the Prosecutor, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: IZET KARAHASANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall on that occasion, because I read that and I made some changes, and that was retyped. Then this lady came, and I signed it in her presence. I remember doing that. Now as to whether somebody talked to me at that time, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Did that lady ever ask you whether had you been coerced to give the statement or whether you had given the statement under duress?

utterances.speaker: IZET KARAHASANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Out of respect for this Tribunal, every time I was summoned to come to Sarajevo, I responded and I cooperated with your investigators. They asked me questions, and I tried and all that. Simply, in a statement, I think the second time when I was there, I don't know whether the investigator's name was Johann or something else, that man really exerted as lot of pressure on me to say this or say that. He said, "Well, it is nothing. This thing that I'm doing to you, it is nothing compared to what will happen to you when you come to court to testify. You simply have to get used to that."

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, but do you recall being asked by that lady whether you were giving your statements freely?

utterances.speaker: IZET KARAHASANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Because since I was there on my own, nobody forced me to come. I wanted to cooperate with this Tribunal. That means that I came and I gave my statement. I gave it freely. Nobody forced me to give the statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask that the statement be admitted in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Robson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: I object, Your Honour. But I think, at the minimum, the Prosecution should submit arguments as to why it should be -- why they're seeking it to be admitted, and then I will respond there due course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Sartorio.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Your Honour, for the sake of presenting all of the facts to Your Honours, and in order to ferret out what is the truth and what is not the truth, I think it is important that the statements be admitted in evidence; then Your Honours will judge the credibility and reliability of the witness, based on his testimony and also based on his prior statements. I think that it is important to seek the truth here, and to have all of the facts before the Court. This witness did sign a 92 bis statement; therefore, it would have been admitted under that, without any objection, and it is important to have all of the facts before the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Robson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: First of all, Your Honour, the Prosecution asks that this statement be admitted into evidence. There are, in fact, four statements, and we have seen a number of them today. I'm not sure which statement the Prosecution is inviting to be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The statement on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Well, that wasn't said, Your Honour, but I will accept --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What statement do we have? You know of four. We don't know of four. We know of this statement on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: If the Prosecution is seeking to tender the statement for admission in order that you can examine it and have -- to consider whether to attach to any weight to the substance of the document, I don't think there is any need for that, Your Honour. The Prosecution has read out the relevant parts to the witness in full today, and he has been given the opportunity to comment and he has commented on it. So by adding this statement into evidence, that would not add anything. The principle before this Tribunal is on oral testimony. We've heard the witness's explanations in respect of the various questions pertaining to this statement, and, therefore, there is absolutely no need to admit this statement into evidence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, the statement will become Exhibit number 1354.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now I would like to move to another statement that you gave to the Tribunal, sir, and this is -- My colleague is on his feet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Robson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Yes Your Honour. Just so that we deal with this completely, it is important to know that the witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are you still talking about that statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We've ruled, Mr. Robson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: I'll deal with it in due course, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's fine. Yes, Madam Sartorio.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: May I have a moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: May the witness be shown P0 6206.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And, sir, this is -- this is the statement we were speaking about a moment ago, where you met with someone from the Office of the Prosecutor, as well as from the Registry, and you were able to make changes or comments with regard to your other statements. Isn't what this document is?

utterances.speaker: IZET KARAHASANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, most probably, yes. Since this is the 19th of October, that should be the statement; and then the signing, that's when I made some changes and so on.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to draw the witness's attention to paragraph 11.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, sir, in paragraph 11, you refer back to paragraph 51, and I'm going to ask you if that was the same paragraph 51 that we just looked at a moment ago from your prior statement?

utterances.speaker: IZET KARAHASANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it does because you can see that every time Arabs are mentioned. It is always said that it is the El Mujahid and the El Mujahed is mentioned, and there were Arabs in El Mujahed, for instance. So I really don't know whether the El Mujahed Unit was there. I mentioned the El Mujahedin Unit, and I said here where ever the El Mujahed is mentioned, Arabs should be mentioned, not the El Mujahed, because I wasn't sure whether there was the El Mujahed unit. I insisted all the time that it should say "Arabs," and that all records should reflect this and should state "Arabs." Now, why this was not done, I don't know, that's not for me to say.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Do you also say in this paragraph that: "I think the Arabs were in the El Mujahed unit, since this was the only unit in our zone of responsibility that had Arabs." Is that contained in that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: IZET KARAHASANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't see that written here anywhere. Paragraph 51, I want it to be stated that the soldiers who had come to the hall in Kesten were Arabs. To my knowledge, I believe that Arabs were in the El Mujahed Unit. Why did I say that, that the Arabs were in that unit? Because those were not -- it was not the soldiers of the BH army that were in the El Mujahed Unit. I had no knowledge of our soldiers being part of the El Mujahed Unit, at least not in our area. I don't know about any other areas.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think this would be a good place to stop, because Mr. Mundis needs a few minutes with the Court. Before that, I would also like to ask that that document be admitted in evidence, this statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are you not through with your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. P0 6206 is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, it will become Exhibit number 1355.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. With the assistance of the usher, I would just very quickly like to hand out a document. I provided copies to the Defence and the legal officer this morning. For reasons that with completely unknown to me, I received a fax on the 1st of April from the Italian Ministry of Justice concerning the Trial Chamber's decision of 27 March. We have had an Italian colleague in OTP do a quick translation of this document. Of course, Judge Lattanzi won't require that. I'm not go into the contents of it, Your Honour. I simply want to draw to Trial Chamber's attention and the attention of the Defence that clearly, as reflected in this document, action has been taken with respect to the Trial Chamber's decision. I have no idea whatsoever why they copied me on this letter and faxed me a copy of this letter. But I did think, since it pertained to the Trial Chamber's decision and the forwarding of that decision to the relevant prosecutorial office in Milan, that I would simply make this document available to the Defence and to the Trial Chamber. Again, I have no reason to know why they would have copied me on this letter, but I just wanted to distribute this letter to all the parties, and that's really all I wanted to draw to the Chamber's attention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much Mr. Mundis. Mr. Mundis, we see that you are -- do you know who Dr. Elio Ramondini is?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I believe, based on the translation, that he is with the Office of the Prosecutor of the Tribunal of Milan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I beg your pardon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The order went to the Italian authorities, and basically my understanding of this is that the Italian authorities at the state level are transferring the Trial Chamber's decision to the authorities in Milan, who would be the ones who would actually be in a position to comply with the Trial Chamber's decision. Again, I have -- to be completely transparent and honest, I have no idea why I was copied on this. I have no idea why the fax came to my office. I am simply, at this point, serving as a conduit to get this letter into the hands of the Defence and the Trial Chamber. It simply appeared on my desk yesterday morning, coming off the fax machine on the evening of the 1st of April. That's as far as I can take this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mundis. Yes, Mr. Robson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could just respond briefly on this. There the Defence takes the view that this is rather disappointing, this response.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: It shows that it is on the 1st of April, some two days ago. It looks as though somebody in Italy actually got around to looking at the Trial Chamber's order and simply faxed it off to the parties. So, it's not encouraging. We would invite the Trial Chamber to take whatever measures, stringent measures, to deal with this. We will be approaching the end of the Defence case in the not to distance future.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Robson. Any other thing to be raised? I guess this would then be the opportune moment to take the adjournment? Court adjourned, to 9.00 tomorrow morning, same courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 4th day of April, 2008, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.47 p.m.,
